Q: How to efficiently make concurrent calls to a local Llama 3.1 model using the ollama-python package? A:

While you already have a decent answer, and hopefully have something working since it's now like 15 months ago, I'll add that...

Concurrency is not the same as throughput: use a queue/worker pattern, measure tokens/sec, be careful with local model saturation, use keep_alive, and don’t assume threading will make one local model generate several responses faster.

Good luck!

Q: How can I write a regex that can find passwords in texts and binary data? A:

Your mission statement was to find passwords in binary stream. You can parse a binary stream but the data as seen by the regex engine is 1 byte per character. That's 0-255 decimal - the byte. That's the ascii / extended ascii ranges. Any password characters would only be discernible as a byte. So in binary, ascii strings are packed sequences of 8-bit binary. There is no decoding into Unicode because those characters are > x100. So you are restricted to ascii. Moreover, you can only match printable sequences between x21-x7e to be a realistic non-whitespace password. With that in mind you could try using just hex constructs \xdd :

(?<![^\x21-\x7e])(?=[\x21-\x7e]*[a-z])(?=[\x21-\x7e]*[A-Z])(?=[\x21-\x7e]*[0-9])(?=[\x21-\x7e]*[\\!-#%-*,-/:;?@\[\]_{}])([\x21-\x7e]{10,500})

expanded

(?<! [^\x21-\x7e] )
(?= [\x21-\x7e]* [a-z] )
(?= [\x21-\x7e]* [A-Z] )
(?= [\x21-\x7e]* [0-9] )
(?= [\x21-\x7e]* [\\!-#%-*,-/:;?@\[\]_{}] )
( [\x21-\x7e]{10,500} )       # (1)

Q: How to convert a string to lower case in Bash A:

I attempted to perform some updated benchmarking using the consensus approach for each utility, but instead of repeating a tiny set many times, I...

  1. fed in a 1.85 GB .txt file that's filled to the brim with multi-byte Unicode characters in UTF-8 encoding,

  2. via the pipe in order to equalize the I/O aspect,

  3. while also enforcing LC_ALL=C for all to ensure a level playing field

  • Both bsd-sed and gnu-sed are rather mediocre, to put it very nicely.

    • I don't even know what bsd-sed was trying to do, as their xxhash doesn't match

  • was python3 trying to do Unicode letter-casing?

    • (even though I already forced the locale setting LC_ALL=C)

  • tr is the most extreme

    1. gnu-tr is, by far, the fastest among all

    2. bsd-tr utterly atrocious

  • Perl is faster than any AWK variant I have, unless you're okay with loading the whole file at once using mawk2 in order to gain a tiny bit over Perl 5:

      2.935s mawk2

    vs

      3.081s perl5

  • within AWK, gnu-gawk appears slowest among the three, mawk 1.3.4 in the middle, and mawk 1.9.9.6 fastest: More than 50% time savings over Gawk

Q: Xcode Cloud: Preparing build for App Store Connect failed A:

In my case, I fixed it by updating both Xcode and macOS to the latest versions. Here’s what I did:

  1. Open Xcode Cloud in App Store Connect

  2. Click “Manage Workflow”

  3. Pick your workflow

  4. In the Environment section, set both Xcode and macOS to “Latest Release”

You can also change this directly in Xcode, in the "Integrate" menu.

Q: Passing a function to `hx-on` for reading the event A:

The event keyword is accessible directly, so you don't need to use lambda function. Also you're missing :: which is a shorter way of accessing htmx events.

Something like this should work (make sure you have the latest htmx js lib version):

hx-on::config-request="console.log('🙌 ', event)"
